column1: # Reviewed differences between the two stds' signature records, each with the
# unit it is due by (`-` for none) and the reason. The lane fails on a
# difference not listed here, on a listed one that is gone, and on any whose

column3: Stage 0 under-reports the effect: the body names a value of an unsafe type (the `None` of the `UnsafePointer<Int8>?` field), and the spec's trigger rule makes a function unsafe when it "names, binds, receives or returns a value of an unsafe type", deliberately broader than "performs a deref"; calling it needs no ceremony, so no caller changes

Stage 0 under-reports the effect, as for `StringBuilder.init`: the body names the `None` of the `UnsafePointer<T>?` field, which the spec's trigger rule makes `unsafe`; calling it needs no ceremony, so no caller changes

SL:borrowing §4 rules a shared twin for `Vector.[]` (`@synthesize(shared)`), which Stage 0's std predates; a read through `v[i]` borrows the root shared instead of exclusively, and getitem derives from the twin as §5.2 requires

The spec declares `value()` with a `@synthesize(shared)` accessor beside it (Shared Ownership), which Stage 0's std predates; a read through it borrows the box shared, so a `let` box and a `&Box` serve `borrow b.value().m()`, the one way a payload method is reached (SL-712)

SL:borrowing §2.4 and K14 rule `get` the optional copy, a plain `&self` value method declared where `T: Copy`, since a public generic declares what it requires, and move the conditional lend to `find`; Stage 0's std predates the ruling and declares the lend under `get`, which sawc2's own source keeps calling
SL:borrowing §2.4 rules `find` the conditional lend, with a `@synthesize(shared)` twin; Stage 0's std predates it and declares no `find`

The error type is `SystemError` (`std.systemerror`), not `IoError` (`std.net`): SL-443 input 3 keeps `std.net`, the runtime's raw-code seam and its pthread-keyed slot out of a file's cone, and the no-abbreviations doctrine names it after the `SysError` tags it reads; the effect (`unsafe`), receiver and parameters are Stage 0's, and the driver and loader only match the Err and print it through `{}`

`read()` takes no `size:` parameter: compiler/ reads whole files only, and the bounded read is a later unit's; the error type is `SystemError`, as for `File.open`; a read returning fewer bytes than asked repeats, and a file that ends before the length lseek(2) reported is `Err(UnexpectedEnd)`, where Stage 0 returns the short prefix

The copy hook is written, not synthesized: the new std's `Data` holds its refcount in its own block (`{ refcount, capacity, bytes }`) rather than in an `Arc<DataBuf>`, so there is no field whose copy a derivation could forward to; the tier is the same, a retain that copies no bytes

Stage 0's `Data` derives `Send` through `Arc<DataBuf>`; the new std's block pointer blocks the derivation, so it is declared, on the grounds `String` declares it: the block is written only by its sole owner and the count is atomic. The trait set a bound sees is the same
As `UnsafeSend`: Stage 0 derives `Sync` through the `Arc`, the new std declares it

New in the new std, replacing `std.net.IoError` for the file seams (SL-443 input 3): the operation's name and a kind, and no platform error number, since the raw code lives in the runtime's pthread-keyed slot
New with `SystemError`; Stage 0's `IoError.kind()` answers the same question with `IoErrorKind`
New with `SystemError`; it renders as `open failed (not found)`, where Stage 0's `IoError` renders `io error: open failed (not found)`
New with `SystemError`, the `Error` conformance's rendering

New with `SystemError`, replacing `IoErrorKind`: the runtime's portable tags under unabbreviated names, plus `UnexpectedEnd` and `LaunchFailed`, which std raises itself; not raw-backed, so a kind std adds takes no number from the frozen tag space
New with `SystemErrorKind`, as `IoErrorKind.describe` is with its kind
The error type is `SystemError`, as for `File.open`; the effect, the parameters and the 0644 permission of a created file are Stage 0's, and the driver only matches the Err and prints it through `{}`

The error type is `SystemError`, as for `File.open`; the by-value `Data` parameter and the byte count are Stage 0's (SL:open-questions, "SL-522 (Stage 0 std)"). A write(2) that takes fewer bytes than offered repeats with the rest and an interrupted one is retried, where Stage 0 returns one write(2)'s count; the driver checks the count against the text's length under both

The error type is `SystemError`, as for `File.open`. Both stds release the descriptor either way, answer a second close with `InvalidArgument`, and report a failing close(2) as `Unknown`, since no runtime seam closes a descriptor and its errno is not captured

Declared in `std.data`, as an extension of `String`, since `std.data` imports `std.string` and the new std refuses an import cycle; the signature is Stage 0's, and a caller imports `std.data` to see it (the driver does, under both stds)

The error type is `SystemError`, as for `File.open`, where Stage 0's is `IoError`; both take the `__saw_rt_executable_path` seam's resolved path, read no errno and report its NULL as `Unknown`, and the driver only matches the Err and prints it through `{}`

The error type is `SystemError`, not `ProcessError`: a spawn's failure carries its cause, the child's exit 127 is `LaunchFailed`, and a NUL inside the program or an argument is `InvalidArgument`, where Stage 0's `ProcessError` names the program and truncates the argument at the NUL. Both block the thread on a doubling sleep over `try_wait` (SL:open-questions, "SL-522 (Stage 0 std)"), and the driver only matches the Err and prints it through `{}`

Stage 0 writes an empty `deinit` body, dead code under design 131; the new std's synthesized drops release the same fields, and neither waits for a child or does anything but free memory (SL:hazards S28)

`public` in the new std's prelude, which a program reaches it through; Stage 0's builtin module declares it bare, and every program sees that module whole. Both are `unsafe` and generic over the `T` held inline (SL:open-questions D38)

The new std writes the one accessor design 186 names, `ptr(&self) unsafe -> UnsafePointer<T>`, as a body over the cell's field; Stage 0's code generator intercepts it, so its builtin module declares none
`public` in the new std's prelude, as for `UnsafeMutableInterior`; both hold the one cell field `value` and are generic over `T` (SL:open-questions D38)

The new std's operations read and write the `Int` word, since v1 atomics are `Atomic<Int>` only and another width is refused where its type is formed (SL:open-questions D38); Stage 0 types them over `T` and lowers every one to an `i64` atomic whatever `T` is. Both are sequentially consistent and take `&self`
As `load`: the new std's `store(&self, v: Int)`, over the `Int` word
As `load`: the new std's `fetch_add(&self, v: Int) -> Int`, over the `Int` word
As `load`: the new std's `compare_exchange(&self, expected: Int, desired: Int) -> Bool`, over the `Int` word

The spec's `SpinLock` section declares `lock()` a `sync borrows(sync) -> &var T` accessor on `&self`, which a `borrow` window takes (SL:borrowing §2.5); Stage 0's std predates `borrow` and declares `lock(body:)`, a `sync` closure whose result comes back out. Both are `unsafe`, `&self`, and release on every way out

The conditional lend of `lock()`, `-> &var T?`, absent when another owner holds the lock, as the spec's `SpinLock` section declares it; Stage 0's std declares `try_lock(body:) -> R?`, the closure form, as for `lock`

The spec's Synchronized Access section declares `lock()` a cell-carrying `(&self) borrows(sync) -> &var T` accessor, as for `SpinLock.lock`; Stage 0's std declares `lock(body:)`, the closure form, released by a scope guard. Both block the thread on the runtime's one-word lock seam

The spec's tier 1 has `SpinLock` declare `ZeroInit` on the condition that `T` does (SL-660), which entitles any module to a bare static of one; Stage 0 has no `ZeroInit` and accepts such a static by its own zero-init rule (SL:hazards L30)
As for `SpinLock`: the spec's tier 1 has `Mutex` declare `ZeroInit` when `T` does; Stage 0 has no `ZeroInit` (SL:hazards L30)
As for `SpinLock`: the spec's tier 1 has `Once` declare `ZeroInit` when `T` does, its zero the unset state; Stage 0 has no `ZeroInit` (SL:hazards L30)

Not raw-backed (the lead's ruling on SL-570): the spec gives the kind no backing, and a tag becomes a kind through `of(tag:)` over std.systemerror's one table of the runtime's tags, as `SystemErrorKind` does; a raw backing would also need `from(raw:)`, which sawc2's backend refuses (SL-540)

Retired (SL-765 c10): a `Void` body's handle is `Thread<Void>`, whose result slot is zero-sized and whose `join()` is a statement. Stage 0 cannot store a `Void` field, which is why it declares the distinct type, and it is frozen
Returns `Result<Int, IoError>` (SL-768): a refused `getsockname` is an `Err`, where Stage 0 answers an `Int` and its frozen std panics on the refusal
Returns `Result<(TcpStream, TcpStream), IoError>` (SL-768): a refused `socketpair` is an `Err`, never two streams with no descriptor, which is what Stage 0's frozen bare pair still hands back
